chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from a man who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy food, and someone comes to me complaining, saying: They have wronged me.' He said: 'Buy it.'

key_terms.ظَلَمُونِي: they have wronged me (claim of debt)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling goods to someone who owes money to others?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the mere existence of debt does not invalidate a commercial transaction, instructing the seller to proceed with the sale even if creditors claim they have been wronged. This ruling underscores the principle of *sahih al-mu'amalat* (validity of transactions) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the debtor's personal liability and the validity of the asset transfer. It reflects the practical flexibility of Shia commercial law, prioritizing the circulation of goods over the immediate settlement of individual debts unless specific conditions of insolvency (*iflas*) are formally established.
